verdict: Neither TWK bot has an edge, on any timeframe, in any year. Both are one indicator: a Supertrend with factor 1.5 and ATR length 10. On gold it flipped 85,968 times in five years of one-minute bars, about 70 times a day. Every flip is a trade for the Pine bot, and the Momentum bot's volume, box and ADX filters are computed from the same price bars, so they thin the trades without changing their sign.

Before costs the system is a coin flip (gross P&L within a few hundred dollars of zero on every timeframe). After XM's spread it is a steady loss: the Pine bot on M1 paid $63,498 in spread to lose $66,887 at 0.02 lot. The best fix candidate, trading only 15:00 to 20:00 server time, still loses on every timeframe. The 95% confidence interval of the average trade is below zero for every base run, so this is not bad luck.

Do not put real money on either bot. At $200 and 0.02 lot every configuration except Momentum M15 wipes the account inside the last six months, which matches what the Strategy Tester did to you on 25 September (balance $7.02 by May 2026).
six_months: The last six months are the worst period in the whole history for the M1 versions, because the one-minute bar is now $2 wide on average against a $0.51 spread. The Momentum bot on M1 took 1,226 trades and lost $1,596; its take-profit was reached in 8% of trades. M15 is the least bad only because it trades 40 times less, not because the logic works better: its profit factor is 0.96 to 0.97 and the bootstrap gives it a 33% to 42% chance of being profitable in a repeat of this period, which is a coin toss with a spread attached.
five_years: Every year is negative for every bot except 2021, where the sample is 7 to 28 trades. The Pine bot on M1 is the clearest picture of the problem: 82,485 trades, a median hold of 5 minutes, 28% winners, and an average trade of -$0.81 with a confidence interval of -$0.86 to -$0.77. The Momentum bot removes 92% of those trades and 92% of the loss, which is what a filter that does not know the future can do at best.

39 of the 61 months are in this run (Dukascopy rate-limited the download mid-session); every calendar year is represented and chunk boundaries are guarded so no trade spans a gap. Re-run run_all.py once the remaining months are in place; the per-year picture will not change sign.
regime: Gold's median price went from $1,787 in 2021 to $4,526 in 2026 and the median one-minute ATR(10) from 35 points to 220 points. Every distance in the bots is a fixed number of points, so the same setting meant a different trade each year. The 500-point hard stop was 14 ATR in 2021 (almost never hit, target too far to reach) and 2.3 ATR in 2026 (hit constantly). The purple-trail activation at 200 points was 6 ATR in 2021 and under one ATR in 2026, so in 2026 nearly every trade trails immediately and gets stopped on the first pullback. The 1:1 trail's 400-point gap is now narrower than an average one-minute bar.

The pivot stop scales the other way: the Momentum bot's 90th-percentile initial risk on M15 grew from about $10 in 2021 to $58 in 2026 at 0.02 lot, and its worst single trade in 2026 lost $200, which is the whole account you tested with.

Simulating the bots with every point distance rescaled by trailing volatility (the volscaled rows in the fixes table) does not rescue them: M1 gets slightly worse, M5 and M15 improve but stay negative. The fixed-point settings were a problem, but the flip logic underneath is the real one.
why: The signal is noise at this frequency. Supertrend(1.5, 10) on a one-minute gold chart flips 70 times a day. Half of all Pine-bot trades end on the purple line within a few minutes; 12% are closed by the next flip; only 8% ever reach the 1:2 target.

Spread is the whole loss on M1. Pine M1: $66,887 lost, $63,498 of it spread. Momentum M1: $5,264 lost, $5,222 spread. Before costs both are flat. A strategy that only loses its transaction costs has no information in it.

The filters are made from the same bars. Buying and selling volume in the Tracker is tick volume split by whether the bar closed up or down, so a LONG flip after green bars nearly always passes the M1 and M3 boxes. ADX above 20 is true after most flips because a flip is a move. Removing every filter (the nofilters row) gives 5 times more trades and 6 times more loss; the filters are a volume knob, not an edge.

The initial stop is structurally wrong. 62% of Momentum M1 trades are quick re-flips (a LONG within 15 minutes of a SHORT). Those take the hard 500-point stop and lost $3,495 of the $5,264 total. The other 38% use a 5-bar pivot that can sit $30 to $80 away on today's gold.

The trailing gives back what the trend gives. On M15 the Momentum bot's exits are 45% by the 1:1 trail and 24% by the purple line versus 6% at the target. It is designed to take small pieces of trends and full-size losses on the stop. Tick-level trailing is harsher than my bar-level replay can show: under the worst-path assumption (the worstpath rows) the M1 loss grows from $5,264 to $7,580.

Position size guarantees ruin. Fixed 0.02 lot with pivot stops means single trades risking 10% to 100% of a $200 account. Every base run except Momentum M15 hits zero from $200 in the last six months alone.
fixes: The session filter (entries 15:00 to 20:00 server time, the London and New York overlap) is the only change that helps every bot on every timeframe, and it still loses: Momentum M1 -$642, M5 -$524, M15 -$298 over five years. Raising the volume ratio back to the default 1.5 halves the trades and the loss on M1 but changes nothing on M15. Reversing on the opposite signal, the setting you used in the 25 September tester run, is the worst variant on every timeframe. The pure Pine strategy (enter only when flat, no trailing) is better than the reverse-on-flip bot but still loses $12,265 on M1.

What would actually be needed is not in the parameter space: a stop capped at a multiple of ATR (skip the trade if the pivot is wider), a trail measured in ATR instead of points, one trade per direction per session, and risk-percent sizing with a hard cap on the stop distance. Even with all of that, the flip itself has to carry an edge, and over five years it does not.
vp: This is the separate test you asked for. Previous-day POC, value-area high and low are built from real one-minute volume; the order-flow gate is the aggressor delta of the last 20 minutes (up-bar volume minus down-bar volume over total), which is the only order-flow signal that exists in five years of history. XM's terminal keeps no depth-of-market history for GOLD, so nobody can backtest a real order-book rule on this symbol, and any vendor claiming to has invented the book.

The rotation playbook (fade a touch of the value-area edge back to the POC, only on days that open inside value) with the order-flow gate is the one thing in this report that is positive over the last six months on all three timeframes: M1 +$184 on 105 trades, M5 +$318 on 88 trades, M15 +$48 on 67 trades. Over five years it is -$1,011 on M1, -$337 on M5 and -$61 on M15 (profit factor 0.98). The gate helps: without it the same playbook is worse on every timeframe over five years. The acceptance playbook (trade the break of the value-area edge) loses everywhere except one small positive on M15 that is within noise.

Read this as: close to zero with costs, better than the TWK bots by a wide margin, and 100 trades of recent profit prove nothing yet. It is worth a demo forward test on M5 or M15; it is not worth real money.
method: Data. Dukascopy XAUUSD one-minute bid candles, UTC shifted to XM server time (EET), prices rounded to XM's 0.01 point. XM's own bars were exported too (M1 back to June 2026, M15 back to July 2022) and used for the spread model: 32 points in 2021 to 2023, 36 in 2024, 38 in 2025, 51 in 2026, which are XM's medians. Swap is XM's: long -86.84 and short +19.79 points per night, triple on Wednesday.

Engine. An exact port of TWK_Core.mqh (Supertrend, 5-bar pivots, up/down volume rows, ADX) drives both bots with their shipped preset values: Momentum ratio 1.2, hard SL 500 points on M1, re-flip within 15 minutes, trail 200/500/100, one position per symbol; Pine reverse on flip, purple trail from the first profitable tick, lock +900 at +1000. Management runs on one-minute bars. Inside a bar a stop is checked before a target, and a trailed stop is tested against the bar's extreme when the bar closes against the trade.

Validation. Against your 25 September Strategy Tester run (M3, ratio 1.5, reverse on opposite): Jan to Feb 2026 tester 118 trades +$61 versus this engine 120 trades +$67 on a different feed, with 77 of the first 120 entry times matching within 3 minutes. In March 2026, when 37% of one-minute bars were wider than the 400-point trail gap, the tester's tick-level trailing exited earlier than any bar replay can, so the Momentum bot is reported under both trailing assumptions and the truth lies between them. Both are negative.

Limits. Dukascopy volume is traded volume, XM's is tick count, so filter decisions differ trade by trade (the ratio-based filters are robust to this, the trade lists are not). 22 months are still missing from the five-year set (2021-10 to 2022-03, 2022-05 to 07, 2022-09, 2023-01, 2023-05, 2023-08, 2024-01, 2024-03, 2024-04, 2024-07, 2024-09 to 11, 2025-01, 2025-12); the download script retries them and run_all.py picks them up automatically. No slippage beyond the spread. The M3 preset was not replayed here because your own tester run already covers it (269 trades, -$193, ruin by May). For a final confirmation on XM's real ticks, run the Strategy Tester on M5 and M15 from 2024-01-02 with a $1,000 deposit and 0.01 lot; the sign will not change.
scenario_exact: The scenario you asked for is negative over five years on every reading, from -$785 (ratio on both rows, 1:2 target) to -$1,603 (no target). Its profit factor is 0.71 to 0.86 and 27% to 28% of trades win. Closing on the opposite flip changes nothing, because with the stop sitting on the purple line the stop is always hit before the line can flip. The one good year is 2026, and even there the money came in January to March, when gold fell from $5,100 to $4,350 and every trend ran for hours; the last six months of the same settings are -$127.

Putting the stop on the purple line from the first tick does fix the two things that were wrong with the stop: no more $30 to $80 pivot stops and no more re-flip stops. It does not fix the entry. With the stop that close, 72% of trades are stopped out, and the winners are not big enough to pay for them plus the spread.
scenario_grid: To answer "make me profitable scenarios" honestly I searched 144 settings around yours (volume ratio 1.2 / 1.5 / 2.0, ADX 20 / 25 / 30, target 1:1 / 1:2 / 1:3 / none, all hours or 15:00 to 20:00, hold or close on flip), tuned on 2021 to 2024 and then checked on 2025 to 2026 without changing anything. Four settings were profitable in the tuning period, by at most $12 on 50 trades. Thirty-eight were profitable in 2025 to 2026. Not one is profitable in both. That pattern is what a strategy with no edge looks like when the market regime changes: whatever fits the calm 2021 to 2024 years loses in the trending 2025 to 2026 years and the other way round.

The best 2025 to 2026 setting (ratio 1.5, ADX 20, target 1:1, entries 15:00 to 20:00) made $403 on 264 trades with a profit factor of 1.24 and $131 in the last six months, but lost $387 with a profit factor of 0.61 on the four years before, and even in its good period the 95% interval of its average trade runs from -$0.47 to +$3.70. If you forward-test anything from this family on demo, test that one, size it at 0.01 lot on at least $1,000, and expect it to stop working when volatility falls. Do not trade it for real on this evidence.
